content.user_title: Reuse Existing Libraries Before Writing Custom Code
content.value_statement: Custom helpers can duplicate existing functionality and increase maintenance work. This skill guides library discovery and direct reuse before implementing only the missing behavior.
actual_capabilities: Directs searches through Effect modules, existing repository dependencies, and npm, in that order.
Provides library recommendations for validation, dates, authentication, SQL, React interfaces, and other common tasks.
Discourages wrappers that only forward calls to existing functions.
Recommends extension APIs and options for behavior that existing solutions do not provide.
Guides package comparisons using maintenance status, type definitions, and dependency count.
Recommends generated Effect API clients or generation from a published OpenAPI specification.
limitations: Provides instructions and reference lists, not executable search or integration tools.
Recommendations emphasize Effect, TypeScript, npm, and React rather than every language ecosystem.
Current package availability and maintenance require external verification.
Does not define a dependency security, licensing, or vulnerability review process.

use_cases.title: Replace Duplicate Helpers
use_cases.description: Check existing dependencies before adding grouping, validation, date, or retry helpers.

use_cases.title: Plan an API Integration
use_cases.description: Look for an existing Effect SDK or an OpenAPI generation route before writing a custom client.

use_cases.title: Review Abstraction Choices
use_cases.description: Identify forwarding wrappers and separate necessary custom behavior from functionality available in maintained libraries.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Reusable Utility
prompt_templates.prompt: I need [operation] in [project]. Check existing dependencies and the library reference before suggesting a new helper.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Library Candidates
prompt_templates.prompt: Find existing solutions for [requirement]. Search Effect modules, repository dependencies, and npm. Compare maintenance, types, and dependency counts.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Proposed Wrapper
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [function or proposal]. Identify forwarding wrappers, recommend direct calls, and reserve custom code for missing behavior. Check extension APIs first.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an Effect API Client
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an Effect integration for [service]. Check @distilled.cloud SDK availability, then published OpenAPI generation options. Identify gaps without inventing package availability.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate SDK reuse and generation.

output_examples.input: Should I write a helper for grouping records?
output: Check whether the repository already provides a grouping utility.
The reference recommends es-toolkit for grouping operations.
Use the existing function directly when it satisfies the requirement.

output_examples.input: How should I choose an Effect client for an external service?
output: Check whether a generated @distilled.cloud SDK exists for the service.
If none exists, check for a published OpenAPI specification and assess @effect/openapi-generator.
Implement only behavior that the selected client and its extension options cannot provide.

output_examples.input: Search summaries do not show a package for my requirement. Should I build it?
output: Inspect the candidate repository packages and npm scope listings directly.
Search using relevant standards, format names, and data names.
Compare maintained candidates before deciding that custom implementation is necessary.

best_practices: Inspect existing modules and dependencies before searching npm or adding custom code.
Verify candidate package listings directly instead of relying only on search summaries.
Check maintenance, types, dependencies, security, and licensing before adopting a package.
anti_patterns: Writing a helper before checking existing implementations.
Adding wrappers that only forward calls without required behavior.
Assuming a missing search summary result proves that no suitable package exists.

faq.question: Does this skill install packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. The supplied files provide guidance and recommendations, not an installer or executable automation.

faq.question: Which ecosystem does it emphasize?
faq.answer: The references emphasize Effect, TypeScript, npm, and React, alongside runtime APIs such as Web Crypto.

faq.question: Where does the search process begin?
faq.answer: It begins with Effect modules, then existing repository dependencies, and finally npm.

faq.question: Is custom implementation always prohibited?
faq.answer: No. The skill permits writing missing behavior and prefers extension APIs or options when available.

faq.question: How does it compare package candidates?
faq.answer: It favors maintained packages with type definitions and fewer dependencies, and recommends inspecting complete package listings.

faq.question: Does a recommendation guarantee package security?
faq.answer: No. The skill does not provide vulnerability checks or a dependency security review process. Evaluate each package before adoption.
